description: Approves a $177.8 million capital plan for 2026-2035.
Funds 10 major projects, including a $65 million East Leisure Center.
Includes $2 million for White Buffalo Youth Lodge design work.

chips.text: East Leisure Center designed for 80,000 future residents in the Holmwood sector.
Councillor Pearce requested current leisure center capacity statistics
Old assessment software poses cybersecurity risks and makes the city susceptible to appeal losses.
Plan includes $2 million for a green networks natural area program under sustainability priorities.
Staff will report back in 2025 with updated East Leisure Center cost estimates.

segments.title: Motion to Approve the Major Capital Funding Plan
segments.takeaway: Councillor DeWall moved the recommendation to approve the 2026-2035 Major Capital Funding Plan as presented.

segments.title: Administration Presentation on Capital Funding Plan
segments.takeaway: Administration presented the 2026-2035 Major Capital Funding Plan, detailing its prioritization process, proposed projects, and funding mechanisms.

segments.title: Council Questions on Capital Projects and Funding
segments.takeaway: Council members questioned administration on specific projects like the East Leisure Center, White Buffalo Youth Lodge, and the Civic Operations Long-Term Project, as well as funding details.

segments.title: Approval of the Major Capital Funding Plan
segments.takeaway: The committee voted to approve the 2026-2035 Major Capital Funding Plan, providing direction for future budget development.

description: Committee recommends $20,000 annual scholarship for watershed initiatives.
Funds repurpose existing Water Utility budget for 2025.

chips.text: Councillor Dubois questioned why the $20,000 was not part of the regular budget process.
Community partners like Meewasin will benefit from the scholarship program.
Funds will support river shoreline enhancements and invasive weed control.
Administration will provide annual updates on the scholarship recipients and their projects.

description: Council reviewed 2026/2027 budget options to reduce future tax increases.
Administration will report on city spending on other governments' responsibilities.

chips.text: Councillor Jeffries questioned the Chamber's data on city spending outpacing inflation.
Saskatoon businesses and taxpayers are affected by potential property tax increases.
Business groups urged Council to control spending, limit tax increases, and explore AI/outsourcing.
Options include funding for affordable housing incentives and homelessness response programs.
Mayor Block promised a business forum and survey for business license holders.

speakers.name: Jason Aebig
speakers.summary: Jason Aebig, Greater Saskatoon Chamber of Commerce, addressed the Committee urging Council to control spending like businesses do, rather than relying on tax increases.
said: Businesses control spending, expect city to do same
City spending outpaced growth, frustrating commercial taxpayers
Demand savings, use AI/outsourcing to reduce tax burden

speakers.name: Keith Moen
speakers.summary: Keith Moen, NSBA, addressed the Committee urging Council to limit tax increases, pursue fiscal restraint, consider workforce reductions and AI adoption, and act on cost-saving recommendations to ensure sustainable city finances.
said: Pace of tax increases is not sustainable
Council must direct administration to find efficiencies
Limit new hires, reduce workforce, embrace AI for savings

segments.title: Administration presents budget options
segments.takeaway: Administration presented the 2026/2027 business plan and budget options, outlining capital and operating options, financial context, and comparisons to other cities.

segments.title: Greater Saskatoon Chamber of Commerce presentation
segments.takeaway: Jason Abick from the Chamber of Commerce urged council to prioritize options that improve direct service, create jobs, and generate economic activity, and to explore real cost reductions.

segments.title: North Saskatoon Business Association presentation
segments.takeaway: Keith Moan from the NSBA highlighted the unsustainability of tax increases, advocating for fiscal prudence, workforce efficiency, and the strategic use of AI to manage staffing levels.

segments.title: Council questions administration on budget report
segments.takeaway: Council members questioned administration on inflation metrics, the property tax model, the financial impact of growth, and the city's current and future plans for AI implementation.

segments.title: Motion for report on other governments' responsibilities
segments.takeaway: Councillor DeBois moved that administration provide a report detailing budget items typically the responsibility of other levels of government but currently funded by the city.

segments.title: Vote on motion for report on funding responsibilities
segments.takeaway: Council voted to approve the motion requesting an information report on budget items typically the responsibility of other levels of government but currently funded by the city.

description: City approved an update to its cybersecurity program.
